verses.12:1: Eu vos darei graças, Senhor, {quoniam}: * {conversus}, e me consolastes.
verses.12:3: Porque o Senhor é a minha força e o meu louvor, * e se fez salvação para mim.
verses.12:4: {gaudio} {haurietis} águas das fontes {salvatoris}: * e direis naquele dia: Dai graças ao Senhor, e invocai o seu nome:
verses.12:5: Fazei conhecer entre os povos as suas {adinventiones}: * lembrai-vos de que o seu nome é excelso.
verses.12:6: Cantai ao Senhor, {magnifice}: * anunciai isto em toda a terra.
verses.12:7: Exulta e louva, {habitatio}: * porque é grande no meio de ti o Santo de Israel.

decisions.why: The Latin gives thanks *because* God was angry: *quóniam* is causal, and nothing marks a concession. The Hebrew (*kî ʾānaptā bî*) is usually read 'though you were angry', and the CNBB LH makes it concessive (*porque, estando irritado, acalmou-se a vossa ira*). DRB keeps the bare causal (*for thou wast angry with me*), and so does MS1932 (*porque te iraste contra mim*), who then adds a bracketed *(mas)* before the second half. We ignore that as one of his glosses (D28). A reader can take the causal two ways: thanks for the anger that led to comfort, or thanks for the whole turn from anger to comfort. The Latin leaves both open, and so does this line (rule 2). *Irásci → irar-se* (the row). The dative *mihi* becomes *contra mim*, as the psalter builds anger against someone (17:8 *irátus est eis → se irou contra eles*; 105:40).

options.label: porque vos irastes contra mim
options.note: Draft. The Latin's causal, bare, as in DRB and MS1932.

options.label: porque vos irastes comigo
options.note: *Irar-se com* is also Portuguese and one syllable shorter, but it is softer than the psalter's *contra*, and nowhere else in the psalter is the dative of anger built this way.

options.label: porque, tendo-vos irado contra mim
options.note: The CNBB LH's concessive build. It decides for 'though' and so resolves what the Latin leaves open. Refused.

decisions.why: *Convértere → voltar* is the glossary's verb. Here its subject is the anger, and the sense is 'turned back, turned away' (DRB *thy wrath is turned away*; Heb. *yāšōb ʾappekā*; the LXX makes God the subject: ἀπέστρεψας τὸν θυμόν σου). Bare *voltou-se o vosso furor* is heard first as the anger turning *towards* someone, which is the opposite sense. *Voltar atrás* keeps the Latin's verb, and *atrás* supplies only the direction Portuguese needs. It is how Brazilians say that something backs off or relents. *Furor → furor* (the row; 73:1). MS1932's *aplacou-se* is another verb, and it names the result instead of the turn.

options.label: o vosso furor voltou atrás
options.note: Draft: the glossary's verb, with the direction supplied. Fifteen syllables for fifteen.

options.label: voltou-se o vosso furor
options.note: Word for word, in the Latin's order. It can be heard as the anger turning towards the speaker.

options.label: o vosso furor se afastou
options.note: Clear. But it is *avértere*'s verb in Ps 84 (84:4 *afastastes-vos da ira*), so it would put another Latin word into the line.

options.label: o vosso furor se aplacou
options.note: MS1932. Another verb (*placáre*); it names the result. Refused.

decisions.why: A verbless clause after *ecce*. It can be read 'Behold, God is my saviour' (DRB, MS1932 *Eis que Deus é o meu Salvador*) or as an apposition, 'Behold God, my saviour'. The predicate reading is the more natural one in Latin, and both Vulgate-family versions take it. Supplying the copula is grammar (D2). *Ecce → eis* (the row). *Salvátor → Salvador* with a capital, as in the row (24:5 *vós sois, Deus, o meu Salvador*). The CNBB LH has the apposition, *Eis o Deus, meu Salvador*, and Brazilian ears know it well. It is kept as an option. Nine syllables for nine.

options.label: Eis que Deus é o meu Salvador

forms.ecce: Eis que Deus é o meu Salvador

options.note: Draft. It supplies the copula, as DRB and MS1932 do.

options.label: Eis Deus, o meu Salvador
options.note: The apposition reading, verbless like the Latin, two syllables shorter. Bare *Eis Deus* is abrupt.

options.label: Eis o Deus, meu Salvador
options.note: The CNBB LH / Lectionary wording (circulation.md). The article makes it 'the God who is my saviour'.

decisions.why: The same two words as 11:6b *fiduciáliter agam in eo → nele agirei com confiança* (the row *fiduciáliter (ágere)*, open). Copied without *nele*, which the Latin here does not have. DRB *I will deal confidently*. MS1932's *viverei cheio de confiança* changes the verb. The CNBB's *eu confio* turns the adverb into the verb and drops *ágere*. Thirteen syllables for thirteen.

options.label: agirei com confiança
options.note: Draft: 11:6b.

options.label: terei confiança
options.note: Plainer to say, but it loses *ágere* and breaks the link with 11:6b.

options.label: confiarei
options.note: The CNBB's *eu confio*, in the future. A paraphrase: the adverb becomes the verb.

decisions.why: *Haurire* is to draw water (L&S). It is not a psalter word (concord). *Tirar água* is the only everyday Brazilian phrase for drawing water from a well or spring, and it is MS1932's verb (*tirareis … águas das fontes*). It shares *tirar* with *auférre* (D41), but here it takes *água*, and the two Latin verbs never meet. The cognate *haurir* is learned ('haurir forças'), and a listener could miss it. The CNBB's *bebereis* is another verb. *Aquas* plural → *águas*, as 17:16a *fontes aquárum → as fontes das águas*.

options.label: tirareis
options.note: Draft; MS1932. The plain verb for drawing water.

options.label: haurireis
options.note: The cognate. It is exact but learned, and it is heard first in the figurative *haurir forças*.

options.label: bebereis
options.note: The CNBB Lectionary refrain. It is another verb. Refused.

decisions.why: *Gáudium → júbilo* is the glossary row (open, for a ruling). 20:7 *in gáudio → de júbilo*, 29:12, 50:10 and 125:2a follow it, and so does canticle 214 (Jer 31:17). *Alegria* is *lætítia*'s word. This canticle has no *lætítia*, but the row is one word across the psalter. The phrase is moved to the head of the verse: *Tirareis águas com júbilo das fontes* would split the waters from their springs. Order is the ear's (D2). The CNBB Lectionary refrain begins the same way (*Com alegria bebereis*).

options.label: Com júbilo
options.note: Draft: the row, fronted.

options.label: Com alegria
options.note: The CNBB's word and the plainest. But it is *lætítia*'s word, so it merges the two nouns.

decisions.why: Jerome wrote *Salvatóris*, the person, where the Hebrew (*ha-yešûʿāh*) and the LXX (τοῦ σωτηρίου) have 'salvation'. The Latin is followed against both (rule 1), with DRB (*the saviour's fountains*) and MS1932 (*das fontes do Salvador*; his note reads it of Christ). It also answers 12:2 *salvátor meus*, which the Latin repeats on purpose. The Brazilian Lectionary refrain has *manancial da salvação*, from the Hebrew (circulation.md). That is the most-sung line of the canticle, and it will be missed.

options.label: do Salvador
options.note: Draft: the Latin's word, capitalised as DO prints it, and matching 12:2.

options.label: da salvação
options.note: The Hebrew, the LXX and the CNBB. It is not what the Latin says. Refused.

decisions.why: *Adinvéntio → invenções* is the row (open; 27:4, 76:13, 80:13, 98:8, 105:29, 105:39), and 76:13 already says it of God (*nas vossas invenções*). It was held there against the stylist, with Gustavo flagged. The Greek here is τὰ ἔνδοξα and the Hebrew *ʿălîlōtāw* (deeds), but the Latin has its own word. DRB (*his works*) and MS1932 (*as suas obras*) both flatten it to works. *Obras* is *ópera*'s word, and *desígnios* is *consílium*'s (D33). So the row is followed, and this is a second place for Gustavo's ruling on it. The CNBB's *maravilhas* is *mirabília*'s word.

options.label: invenções
options.note: Draft: the row, as 76:13 (God's).

options.label: obras
options.note: DRB, MS1932. The plainest word, but it is *ópera*'s.

options.label: desígnios
options.note: 76:13's stylist asked for it. It is *consílium*'s word (D33).

decisions.why: *Magnífice fecit*: 'he has done magnificently', with *fácere* used absolutely (DRB *he hath done great things*; MS1932 *porque ele fez coisas magníficas*; the LXX ὑψηλὰ ἐποίησεν). Portuguese cannot leave *fez* without an object, so either the verb becomes 'act' or an object is supplied. *Agiu com magnificência* keeps the adverb's root, as the row *magnificéntia → magnificência* has it, and adds no noun. It ends on a paroxytone at the mediant, where *magníficas* would give a proparoxytone (rule 4). Cost: *agir* also stands for *agam* in 12:2 (*fácere* and *ágere*, two verbs in the Latin). Fifteen syllables for fifteen.

options.label: porque agiu com magnificência
options.note: Draft. It keeps the root, and the mediant cadence is correct.

options.label: porque fez coisas magníficas
options.note: MS1932. The most natural to say, and it keeps *fez*. It supplies a noun, and it puts a proparoxytone at the mediant.

options.label: porque fez grandes coisas
options.note: DRB. It is plain, but it drops the splendour of *magnífice*.

decisions.why: The address is to Sion's 'dwelling', a feminine singular that stands for those who live there (the Hebrew *yôšebet ṣîyôn*, 'she who dwells in Zion'; the LXX οἱ κατοικοῦντες Σιων). The Latin keeps the abstract noun and the singular. So the imperatives are singular *tu* (rule 3: *Exulta e louva*, *no meio de ti*), as MS1932 has them. *Habitátio → habitação* is the row (75:3 *e a sua habitação em Sião*). The CNBB *habitantes de Sião* is the Hebrew-family plural, and MS1932's *casa* is another noun. The vocative has no *ó*, as the glossary keeps it where the Latin has no *o*.

options.label: habitação de Sião
options.note: Draft: the row. The two *-ão* endings chime inside the colon; the mediant and the final do not rhyme.

options.label: morada de Sião
options.note: It avoids the internal chime, but *morada* is *habitáculum*'s word (D44).

options.label: casa de Sião
options.note: MS1932. It is *domus*'s word.

choices.12:1: DO's first line, *(Canticum Isaiæ * Isa 12:1-7)*, is a heading with the book reference. It is not a prayed verse and not a titulus. readVerses skips it, as it did for 213 and the Nunc dimittis, and D7 keeps tituli out anyway. The Vulgate's lead-in *Et dices in die illa* is not part of DO's text. *Confitébor tibi, Dómine* → *Eu vos darei graças, Senhor* (D5; the formula of 9:2, 110:1, 137:1a). The DO ids run 12:1–12:7 because DO splits Vulgate 12:2 in two, so from 12:3 on they run one ahead of the Vulgate. The Latin is Jerome's Isaiah from the Hebrew, not the Gallican psalter.
choices.12:3: The same words as 117:14 (*Fortitúdo mea, et laus mea Dóminus: * et factus est mihi in salútem*), with *Quia* in front. Copied: *O Senhor é a minha força e o meu louvor: * e se fez salvação para mim*, where *Dóminus* is moved up so that the subject comes first (the 117:14 ruling; the glossary's formula row names this canticle id). *Quia → Porque*. Canticle 224 (Ex 15:2) has the same line.
choices.12:4: *Et dicétis in die illa: Confitémini Dómino, et invocáte nomen ejus* copies 104:1 *Dai graças ao Senhor, e invocai o seu nome* (D5). *In die illa → naquele dia* (145:4). Like the Latin, the line has no quotation marks: where the people's speech ends is left open (the CNBB closes it at the end of the canticle).
choices.12:5: *Notas fácite → Fazei conhecer* (the *notum fácere* row: 97:2, 144:12). *In pópulis → entre os povos* (56:10, 107:4). *Mementóte → lembrai-vos* (104:5), with *de que* for *quóniam*, the standard build. *Excélsum → excelso* (D43).
choices.12:6: *Cantáte Dómino → Cantai ao Senhor* (95:1). *Annuntiáte → anunciai* (D41). *In univérsa terra → em toda a terra* (8:2a).
choices.12:7: *In médio tui → no meio de ti* (115:9, a place addressed). *Sanctus Israël → o Santo de Israel* (70:22, 77:41). *Porque é grande no meio de ti o Santo de Israel* keeps the Latin's order and both readings of it: 'the Holy One is great in your midst' and 'great is he who is in your midst' (DRB). The CNBB has the same order.

audit.note: Canticle-level draft. parallels.py handles only psalm numbers, so ps221/show_parallels.py (adapted from ps213's) builds consult/parallels/ps221.md from: the DO Latin; the Bolls Vulgate, WLC Hebrew and DRB of Isaiah 12 (consult/ps221/bolls-*-23-12.json); the Rahlfs LXX from consult/lxx-*.csv; drbo.org's Isaias 12 page; and Matos Soares 1932 from the pdftotext text layer of the 1932 PDF, p. 1458 (consult/ps221/ms1932-isaiah12.txt). There is no Diurnal: the canticle is not in it. Precedent was checked with ps221/concord.py (ps213's, renamed) and glossary rows with ps221/gloss.py. Brazilian circulation was fetched and recorded in ps221/circulation.md: the CNBB LH prays it at Thursday Lauds of Week II, and the Lectionary uses it at the Easter Vigil, on the Sacred Heart (B) and on Advent III (C), in a paraphrase from the Hebrew. Copied from finished psalms: 117:14 (12:3), 104:1 (12:4b), 11:6b (*agirei com confiança*), the *Confitébor tibi, Dómine* formula. Hard readings: the causal *quóniam irátus es*, *convérsus est furor*, *Salvatóris* against the Hebrew's 'salvation', *adinventiónes* of God, *magnífice fecit*.

Hard checks pass: ids and marks match DO's Latin. render.py and checks.py ran unchanged with the DO number 221, and readVerses skips the heading line. One soft flag, accepted: 12:4b is 3 syllables short of a 26-syllable colon, because it copies 104:1 and needs no filler. Every colon ends on an oxytone or paroxytone. 12:6a *magnificência* was chosen partly for that (see decision magnifice).
